title: Big bands on stage with featured dancers
summary: The interviewers and Green agree this was the peak of Chuck and Chuckles, headlining with big bands now moved from the pit onto the stage.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: So, now Chuck, you and Chuckles were

really blooming after all your -- taking all your classes and you developed now fully into a great first-class act, and mostly you headlined with big bands which were also in the vogue at this particular time. Wouldn't you say so?
The arrow was changing, wasn't it? It was moving from one entertainment form to another for tap dancers.
It was going through a transition.
Yes, it was. Yes. Performers were more plentiful and more fully developed, and they were happy with each other. They were happy with the entire profession of show business.
Big bands -- now, this seemed to be the style of the big bands now. A well-known big band usually -- always took a couple of great singers and a great dancing act or a great dancer with them.
And, of course, you now were at this -- this was your peak.
You were fully developed. You'd left Buck and Bubbles.
Yes. And they -- what they had done, you see, they eventually started to putting the bands up on
stage where before they would generally play in the orchestra pit as they called it.
